findings.issue: Teaching color theory before haircolor formulation is more naturally 'theory before practice' or 'simple to complex'; 'known to unknown' wins only because the other options are reversed or nonsense. Color theory is not something students already know.
findings.fix: Reword the stem so the key is clearly known-to-unknown, e.g. 'Reviewing hair structure, which students already studied, before introducing porosity testing applies which principle?', and replace 'Fast to slow' with 'Simple to complex' only if the stem then rules it out.

findings.issue: Distractors 'Fear of detention', 'Stickers on a chart', 'Strict seating rules' are childish strawmen for an adult-learner item.
findings.fix: Use plausible extrinsic motivators: 'Avoiding a low grade', 'Praise from the instructor', 'Competing with classmates'.

findings.issue: 'That time is flexible', 'To arrive a bit late', 'Theory matters less' are easy rejects.
findings.fix: e.g. 'Respect for the instructor's authority', 'That lateness lowers grades', 'How to plan their own day'.

findings.issue: Three distractors are unsafe behaviours ('Skip safety steps', 'Ignore class rules', 'Use tools untrained'); the key is found by elimination.
findings.fix: Use plausible but incomplete answers: 'Work without supervision once trained', 'Choose their own safety steps', 'Avoid all chemical services'.

findings.issue: 'Cleaning is optional', 'Rules are relaxed' are strawmen.
findings.fix: e.g. 'Where supplies are kept', 'That staff do the cleaning', 'How the school is inspected'.

findings.issue: Category-jargon cue: distractors 'Lesson timing', 'Supply inventory', 'Room layout' are clearly unrelated to favoritism. Same pattern in PRO-025 ('Inventory control', 'Lesson sequence', 'Room layout'), PRO-026 ('Lesson timing', 'Test blueprint', 'Par levels') and ENV-017 ('Norm referencing', 'Inventory control', 'Summative assessment').
findings.fix: Use same-domain distractors: PRO-002 'Reliability', 'Confidentiality', 'Academic advising'; PRO-025 'FERPA privacy', 'Satisfactory progress rules', 'Test validity'; PRO-026 'FERPA', 'Copyright', 'Academic integrity'; ENV-017 'Remediation', 'Differentiated grading', 'Peer tutoring'.

findings.issue: All three distractors are obviously dismissive quotes.
findings.fix: Make one or two distractors well meant but not empathetic, e.g. 'Let me just show you again.' and 'You'll get it if you practice tonight.'

findings.issue: Option A 'Counsel them yourself' switches to second person in a third-person stem.
Key is right as instructor practice, but FERPA 99.31(a)(8) lets a school disclose to parents of a tax-dependent student without consent; explanation's 'unless a FERPA exception applies' covers it.
findings.fix: None required; optionally say 'the instructor should not release them and should refer the parent to the records office'.

findings.issue: Many items have one sensible option and three easy rejects (as the builder warned); the items above are the clearest. Keys are evenly spread A/B/C/D (50 each), which is fine since options shuffle on screen.
findings.fix: Sweep distractors in LRN, OBS, TIM, ENV, PRO and SAF for strawmen in a later pass.

landing_findings.issue: Format (85 items, 75 scored, 90 minutes, four options, one correct), domains 33/33/34, CIB effective Dec 1 2024 revised Jan 1 2026, and South Carolina's 80% instructor pass mark all match the official pages fetched 2026-11-18.
Line ~246 tells readers to 'aim for 90% or better on every one before you book', while the tests, FAQ and examFacts use an 80% readiness line. Not false, but mixed message.
landing_findings.fix: Say 'aim to clear the 80% line comfortably, ideally 90%, on every test'.

landing_findings.issue: Hero subtitle ends 'Free to start, no account needed.' and offers come from examOffers(); no 'everything free' claim found.
